2607.13597.title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations
2607.13597.paper_summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, yet fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. A fundamental question therefore arises: what constitutes a good action representation? Inspired by the mirror neuron theory's insight that observation and execution share an intention-level encoding, we examine whether a robot's action representations preserve the semantic structure captured by pretrained encoders. Systematic probing confirms that this structure erodes during finetuning, and that its quality synchronizes with both task success and out-of-distribution generalization. We further introduce a plug-and-play method that anchors action representations to a semantic manifold while decomposing representations into a shared semantic channel and a private channel, all discarded at inference, leaving the deployed model unchanged. Validated on different VLA backbones across simulation and real-world benchmarks, our method yields up to +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization.
2607.13597.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言-行動 (VLA) 模型從預訓練的視覺-語言模型中繼承了豐富的語義表示，但在有限的機器人示範上進行微調會削弱這一結構並損害泛化能力。 因此，一個根本性問題出現了：什麼構成了一個好的行動表示？ 受到鏡像神經元理論的啟發，該理論指出觀察和執行共享一種意圖級別的編碼，我們檢查機器人的行動表示是否保留了預訓練編碼器捕獲的語義結構。 系統性的探測確認這一結構在微調過程中會侵蝕，並且其質量與任務成功和分佈外泛化同步。 我們進一步介紹了一種即插即用的方法，將行動表示固定在語義流形上，同時將表示分解為共享語義通道和私有通道，所有這些在推理時都被丟棄，保持部署模型不變。 在不同的 VLA 骨幹上進行驗證，無論是在模擬還是真實世界基準上，我們的方法在真實世界的內部分佈任務上提高了最多 +18.7%，在分佈外泛化上提高了 +21.5%。
